item.title: How Are Smartphones Exacerbating Our Longing for Expressive Individualism?
item.description: It’s already a problem and a fleshly temptation to want to express an individualistic sense of who you are and what you believe. Social media gives you a megaphone and invites you to do that.

item.title: Worship Service Liturgies for Your Palm Sunday, Good Friday, and Easter Sunday Services
item.description: The Sing! Hymnal can help leaders design a theologically robust and spiritually enriching service. Here are a few examples of thoughtfully composed Holy Week services for your church.

item.title: ​​6 Tactics for Your Fight Against Sin
item.description: In Romans 6:12–13, Paul applies the truth of union with Christ directly to our battle with temptation. He offers a practical strategy for fighting sin that we can break down into six tactics.

item.title: How Are We Supposed to Rest on Sunday?
item.description: Sabbath rest isn’t merely for resting alone in the Lord. It’s for resting with all who also belong to him. It’s for resting with the church.

item.title: Introducing a New Decide-as-You-Go Adventure Series for Kids
item.description: Kids choose the course of this fast-paced sea voyage, the first interactive novel from Kathryn Butler’s the Lamplight Series.

item.title: Why Being Alone Is So Deadly
item.description: The comfort of the good shepherd’s presence is all the more wonderful when we take seriously the reality of the darkness and the presence of evil.

item.title: Podcast: Practical Tips to Help You Pray More (Courtney Reissig)
item.description: Courtney Reissig discusses the importance of prayer and how prayer helps us trust God by coming to him in a posture of dependency.

item.title: Taking a Closer Look at Romans 6
item.description: If you have ever struggled to understand this chapter, just know you’re not alone. Martyn Lloyd-Jones wrestled with these verses too, but he found the wrestling to be very rewarding.

item.title: If Someone Asked You What the Bible Is About, What Would You Say?
item.description: No human being, no matter how brilliant, insightful, or experienced, would have been able to write the grand biblical story. God chooses to surprise us again and again.
